findings.observation: Recorded by the crafter in runs/craft.S3.json (second pass, blocked_by product): with the menu open on the second Overview table at 375 px the scroller jumps to scrollLeft 340 right after the menu item takes focus; the oracle check (before 1ebc516de) failed at 0 expected, 340 received; cause not located after three passes. Still present at HEAD: the oracle no longer checks it (oracle finding 1), so the declared falsifier now passes only because it is unobserved. Candidate location for the mover, unverified: the grid root onFocus (scrollFocusedCellIntoView) at DataGridBase.tsx:552 is reached by focus events inside React's tree, and RowActionsMenu only stops focus at the Paper and the button.
findings.remediation: Locate the mover with a scrollLeft write log and focus log during open (native browser run by the host). Fix so that opening and closing the menu leaves scrollLeft and the edge cues unchanged. Then the restored oracle polls must pass. Do not paper over with a scroll-back in the check.

findings.obligation: Design and one owner per rule (nw-code-craftsmanship semantic DRY; the menu must list exactly the actions the icons offered, in the same order). Original Request: the menu offers the same actions the icons did.
findings.observation: Clone is gated twice. Desktop icon: DataOverviewTable.tsx:284 "(api === \"teams\" || api === \"portfolios\") && canCloneRow(row)". Phone menu: DataOverviewTable.tsx:239 "onClone={canCloneRow(row) ? () => handleClone(row) : undefined}" with no api guard. handleClone is a no-op for any other api. Latent only: the two Overview callers pass api teams and portfolios (pages/Overview/OverviewDashboard.tsx:435-455). If a third api reaches the table with canCloneRow true, the phone menu offers Clone while the desktop shows no Clone icon.
findings.remediation: Derive one predicate (canCloneHere(row) = api is teams or portfolios and canCloneRow(row)) and use it for both the icon and the menu item. Non-blocking for this phase.

findings.obligation: P12 keyboard exposure: the actions are usable with the keyboard, and the keyboard reaches the grid as it does at desktop width (the desktop icons let arrow keys move within the grid). Not a stated acceptance clause; a parity question for the menu button.
findings.observation: RowActionsMenu.tsx: the menu button's onKeyDown is keepFromTheGrid (stopPropagation), so any key pressed on the focused button, arrows included, is stopped before it reaches the grid. Desktop icons do not stop keydown. Not verified in a browser (no Playwright run here); read from the source only.
findings.remediation: Stop only the keys the menu button consumes (Enter, Space) and let navigation keys reach the grid; verify with a keyboard walk on the host. Non-blocking.
